content.title: About
content.content: Rugelach are small baked pastries made from a yeasted dough, traditionally filled with nuts, chocolate, jam, or cheese. The dough is tender and slightly sweet, while the filling adds a rich, aromatic flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rugelach originate from Eastern European Jewish cuisine and are often served at holidays.
They are traditionally shaped into a crescent, though round versions also exist.
The classic recipe uses butter, but modern versions may incorporate vegetable fats.
Fillings can be sweet (chocolate, nuts) or savory (cheese, spinach).
Rugelach are frequently topped with sugar sprinkles or nut crumbs.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: They provide carbohydrates and a modest amount of fat, delivering quick energy.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeasted dough contains thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Nut and dried‑fruit fillings add magnesium, iron, and zinc.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Chocolate and nut fillings are high in polyphenols, which combat free radicals.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: If the filling includes dried fruit, it can help promote regular bowel movements.

items.title: Nut and gluten allergy
items.content: Fillings often contain nuts, and the dough is wheat‑based, which may trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sweet versions can raise blood glucose levels when consumed in excess.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Rugelach are relatively calorie‑dense due to fats and sugar, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rugelach can be enjoyed as a standalone dessert, served with tea or coffee, or used as a sweet snack at celebrations. They are conveniently stored in an airtight container to stay soft.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep rugelach in a dry, cool place in a sealed container for up to 5 days. For longer storage, refrigerate them, where they remain fresh for up to 2 weeks.
